title: Use the Well-Architected Framework, properly
oneliner: Every cloud and enterprise has a Well-Architected Framework - operational excellence, reliability, security, performance, cost - and architects should design against it deliberately.
says: The Well-Architected Framework exists in every organization, public cloud or private enterprise. Solution, cloud, and enterprise architects should use it to design systems. It covers five or six major areas depending on the organization: operational excellence, reliability, security, performance optimization, and cost optimization - varying per organization.
explained: The framework's real value is that it converts 'is this a good design?' from an argument into a checklist with agreed pillars. AWS, Azure, and Google each publish their version; large enterprises adapt their own. When a review runs against the pillars, feedback becomes specific - 'the reliability pillar's failover question is unanswered' - instead of taste.

Notice the pillars rhyme with his very first reel: the -ilities, formalized. Reliability, security, performance, and cost are four of the fifteen. The arc from reel #1 to this one is the channel in miniature: the vocabulary of quality, learned early, becoming the review discipline of a senior architect. AI workloads get reviewed against the same pillars - with token economics under cost and GPU topology under performance.
takeaway: Adopt your cloud's Well-Architected pillars as your design-review template - including for AI systems, where cost and performance have new meanings.
